[2 Ch 19:10](https://ref.ly/2Chr19:10), [19:10](https://ref.ly/2Chr19:10); וַיֶאְשְׁמוּ אָשׁוֺם *and they committed lasting wrong* (irreparable wrong, the Edomites against Judah) Ez [25:12](https://ref.ly/Ezek25:12). **2\.** *be* or *become guilty* Ju [21:22](https://ref.ly/Judg21:22), [Je 50:7](https://ref.ly/Jer50:7), [Ho 4:15](https://ref.ly/Hos4:15), Hb [1:11](https://ref.ly/Hab1:11); in offences requiring sin\-offering [Lv 4:13](https://ref.ly/Lev4:13), [4:22](https://ref.ly/Lev4:22), [4:27](https://ref.ly/Lev4:27) (P), of trespass\-offering [Lv 5:2](https://ref.ly/Lev5:2), [5:3](https://ref.ly/Lev5:3), [5:17](https://ref.ly/Lev5:17), [5:23](https://ref.ly/Lev5:23), [Nu 5:6](https://ref.ly/Num5:6) (P); with ל *guilty of* [Lv 5:4](https://ref.ly/Lev5:4), [5:5](https://ref.ly/Lev5:5) (P), with ב *in* or *through* Ez [22:4](https://ref.ly/Ezek22:4), [Ho 13:1](https://ref.ly/Hos13:1). **3\.** *be held guilty, bear punishment* [Psalm 34:22](https://ref.ly/Ps34:22), [34:23](https://ref.ly/Ps34:23), [Pr 30:10](https://ref.ly/Prov30:10), [Is 24:6](https://ref.ly/Isa24:6), [Je 2:3](https://ref.ly/Jer2:3), [Ho 5:15](https://ref.ly/Hos5:15), [10:2](https://ref.ly/Hos10:2), [14:1](https://ref.ly/Hos14:1), [Zc 11:5](https://ref.ly/Zech11:5), Ez [6:6](https://ref.ly/Ezek6:6) (but cf. שָׁמֵם). **Niph.** נֶאְשָׁמוּ *suffer punishment* [Jo 1:18](https://ref.ly/Joel1:18). **Hiph.** *Impf.* sf. הַאֲשִׁימֵם *declare them guilty* [Psalm 5:11](https://ref.ly/Ps5:11).

> \[Str818] † אָשֵׁם **adj.** guilty, ´א abs. [2 S 14:13](https://ref.ly/2Sam14:13); pl. אֲשֵׁמִים אֶל־אָחִינוּ [Gn 42:21](https://ref.ly/Gen42:21) (E); *guilty*, and so bound to offer a trespass\-offering [Ezr 10:19](https://ref.ly/Ezra10:19); but rd. prob. וַאֲשָׁמָם, so KueChronol. v. h. Perzische Tijdvak, 1890, 43\.

> \[Str817] אָשָׁם **n.m.** offence, guilt—´א [Gn 26:10](https://ref.ly/Gen26:10) \+ 37 t., sf. אֲשָׁמוֺ [Nu 5:7](https://ref.ly/Num5:7) \+ 7 t.;—**1\.** *offence, trespass, fault* [Psalm 68:22](https://ref.ly/Ps68:22) (*guiltiness* RV). **2\.** *guilt* [Gn 26:10](https://ref.ly/Gen26:10) (J) [Pr 14:9](https://ref.ly/Prov14:9), [Je 51:5](https://ref.ly/Jer51:5). **3\.** *compensation*, לְהָשִׁיב הָאָשָׁם אֵלָיו *to whom to return the compensation* (or satisfaction for injury) [Nu 5:7](https://ref.ly/Num5:7), [5:8](https://ref.ly/Num5:8) (P; *restitution for guilt* RV). **4\.** *trespass\-offering* (AV, but *guilt\-offering* RV) used only in Lv 5, [6:10](https://ref.ly/Lev6:10), 7, 14, [19:21](https://ref.ly/Lev19:21), [19:22](https://ref.ly/Lev19:22), Nu 5, [6:12](https://ref.ly/Num6:12), [18:9](https://ref.ly/Num18:9) (P), \& Ez [40:39](https://ref.ly/Ezek40:39), [42:13](https://ref.ly/Ezek42:13), [44:29](https://ref.ly/Ezek44:29), [46:20](https://ref.ly/Ezek46:20), cf. [Ezr 10:19](https://ref.ly/Ezra10:19). This offering seems to have been confined to offences against God or man that could be estimated and so covered by compensation. The ordinary trespass\-offering was a ram, together with restitution and a penalty of a fifth of its value. The trespass\-offerings of the leper and Nazirite were he\-lambs Lv 14, [Nu 6:12](https://ref.ly/Num6:12); if the person who suffered wrong or his kinsmen were not living the fine went to the priests. The victims were offered, the blood and fat pieces going to the altar, the skin and flesh to the priests. There seems to have been no application of the blood to the horns of the altar (the chief ceremony of the sin\-offering) because the guilt was not expiated at the altar but by compensation to the wronged person or his representative. A part of the blood of the leper's trespass\-offering was applied to his person to consecrate him (as in the case of the ram of consecration to consecrate the priests [Lv 8:23](https://ref.ly/Lev8:23)). The trespass\-offering is unknown to JED and the older Hebrew literature. However, the Philistines send an אשׁם of golden mice and tumours [1 S 6:3](https://ref.ly/1Sam6:3), [6:4](https://ref.ly/1Sam6:4), [6:8](https://ref.ly/1Sam6:8), [6:17](https://ref.ly/1Sam6:17), and an אשׁם of money was given to the priests [2 K 12:17](https://ref.ly/2Kgs12:17), but these are entirely different from the trespass\-offering of P. The Messianic servant offers himself as an אשׁם in compensation for the sins of the people, interposing for them as their substitute [Is 53:10](https://ref.ly/Isa53:10) (incorrectly, *sin\-offering* AV RV). See further OehlerOT Theol. § 137 Di [Lv 5:14](https://ref.ly/Lev5:14).

## אֲשֶׁר (id: BDB00939)

\[Str834] אֲשֶׁר **part. of relation** (Moab. *id.;* origin dub.: **1\.** acc. to TsepreghiDiss. Lugd. p. 171 MühlauBö. Lb. ii. 79 n. StaMorg. Forsch. 1875, 188; La. § 167 HommelZMG 1878, 708 ff. Müll:§ 153 SayceHbr. ii. 51 LagM. i. 255 \& esp. KraetzschmarHbr. vi. 298 ff, orig. a subst. ‘ place ’ \= أَثَرٌ *footstep, mark*, አሠር፡ (do.), אֲתַר, ܐܰܬܰܪ *place*, As. *asûru*, used (v. Kraetz.) both as a subst. ‘ there, where, ’ and as a relative of place ‘ where ’: in Heb. this development has advanced further, and it has become a relative sign generally. The chief objection to this explanation is that it would isolate Heb. from the other Semitic languages, in which pronouns are formed regularly from *demonstrative* roots (cf. also NöZMG 1886, 738\). **2\.** according to PhiSt. C. 73 SperlingNota Rel. im Hebr. 1876, 15–22 for אֲשֶׁל, developed from the relative שׁ (q.v.) by (1\) the prefixing of either a merely prosthetic א, or, better, a pronominal א (giving rise to אש, the form of the relative in Ph.), and (2\) the addition of the demonstr. root ל \[found also in אֵל, אֵלָּה, הַלָּזֶה (q.v.), أَلَّدِي *he who*, እለ፡ *who* (pl.)]: the main objection to this explanation is the change of ל to ר, which is hardly rendered probable by the comp. of Syr. ܗܳܪܟܳܐ by side of Targ. הָלְכָּא. **1** seems preferable, the primitive root having acquired different significations in the different Semitic languages, and having been weakened in Heb. to a mere particle of relation). A **sign of relation**, bringing the clause introduced by it into relation with an antecedent clause. As a rule אֲשֶׁר is a mere **connecting link**, and requires to be supplemented (see the grammars) by a pron. affix, or other word, such as שָׁם, defining the nature of the relation more precisely: e.g. [Gn 1:11](https://ref.ly/Gen1:11) אֲשֶׁר זַרֵעוֺ־בוֺ lit. *as to which*, its seed is in it \= in which is its seed, [Psalm 1:4](https://ref.ly/Ps1:4) like the chaff אֲשֶׁר־תִּדְּפֶנּוּ רוּחַ *as to which*, the wind drives it \= which the wind drives, etc.; \& so שָׁם…אֲשֶׁר \= *where*, מִשָּׁם…אֲשֶׁר \= *whence*, [Gn 2:11](https://ref.ly/Gen2:11), [3:23](https://ref.ly/Gen3:23), [20:13](https://ref.ly/Gen20:13) etc. Sometimes also (v. infr.) the relation expressed by it is specifically temporal, local causal, etc. More particularly

 **1\.** it includes its pronominal antecedent, whether in the nom. or obl. cases, as [Nu 22:6](https://ref.ly/Num22:6) וַאֲשֶׁר תָּאֹר יוּאָר and *he whom* thou cursest is cursed, [Ex 4:12](https://ref.ly/Exod4:12) and I will teach thee אֲשֶׁר תְּדַבֵּר *that which* thou shalt say; and with particles or prepositions, as אֵת אֲשֶׁר (acc. to the context) *him who…, those who…, that which…;* לַאֲשֶׁר to *him who…* [Gn 43:16](https://ref.ly/Gen43:16), to *those who…* [47:24](https://ref.ly/Gen47:24), to *that which* [27:8](https://ref.ly/Gen27:8); מֵאֲשֶׁר Ju [16:30](https://ref.ly/Judg16:30), [2 S 18:18](https://ref.ly/2Sam18:18) *than those* whom; [Lv 27:24](https://ref.ly/Lev27:24) לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ מֵאִתּוֺ *to him* from whom he bought it, [Nu 5:7](https://ref.ly/Num5:7); [Is 24:2](https://ref.ly/Isa24:2) כַּאֲשֶׁר נשֶׁא בוֺ *like him* against whom there is a creditor. **2\.** instances of אֲשֶׁר followed by a pron. affix, or by שָׁם, שָֽׁמָּה, מִשָּׁם, are so common that the exx. cited above will be sufficient. Very rarely there occurs the anomalous constr. עִם אֲשֶׁר [Gn 31:32](https://ref.ly/Gen31:32) for אֲשֶׁר עִמּוֺ (see [Gn 44:9](https://ref.ly/Gen44:9)), בַּאֲשֶׁר [Is 47:12](https://ref.ly/Isa47:12) for אֲשֶׁר בָּהֶם, לַאֲשֶׁר for לָהֶם…אֲשֶׁר Ez [23:40](https://ref.ly/Ezek23:40): [Psalm 119:49](https://ref.ly/Ps119:49) see under על אשׁר. It is followed by the pron. in the *nomin.*, in the foll. cases:—(*a*) immediately, mostly before an adj. or ptcp., [Gn 9:3](https://ref.ly/Gen9:3) all moving things אֲשֶׁר הוּא־חַי which are living, [Lv 11:26](https://ref.ly/Lev11:26), [Nu 9:13](https://ref.ly/Num9:13), [14:8](https://ref.ly/Num14:8), [14:27](https://ref.ly/Num14:27), [35:31](https://ref.ly/Num35:31), [Dt 20:20](https://ref.ly/Deut20:20), [1 S 10:19](https://ref.ly/1Sam10:19) (v. Dr) [2 K 25:19](https://ref.ly/2Kgs25:19) (‖ [Je 52:25](https://ref.ly/Jer52:25) היה) [Je 27:9](https://ref.ly/Jer27:9), Ez [43:19](https://ref.ly/Ezek43:19), [Hg 1:9](https://ref.ly/Hag1:9), [Ru 4:15](https://ref.ly/Ruth4:15), [Ne 2:18](https://ref.ly/Neh2:18), [Ec 7:26](https://ref.ly/Eccl7:26); before a vb. [2 K 22:13](https://ref.ly/2Kgs22:13) (omitted [2 Ch 34:21](https://ref.ly/2Chr34:21)). (*b*) in a *negative* sentence, at the end: [Gn 7:2](https://ref.ly/Gen7:2), [17:12](https://ref.ly/Gen17:12), [Nu 17:5](https://ref.ly/Num17:5), [Dt 17:15](https://ref.ly/Deut17:15) אֲשֶׁר לאֹ אָחִיךָ הוּא who is not thy brother, [20:15](https://ref.ly/Deut20:15), Ju [19:12](https://ref.ly/Judg19:12), [1 K 8:41](https://ref.ly/1Kgs8:41) ‖ [9:20](https://ref.ly/1Kgs9:20) ‖. N.B. [Psalm 16:3](https://ref.ly/Ps16:3) אֲשֶׁר בָּאָרֶץ הֵָמָּה is an unparalleled expression for ‘ who are in the land ’; rd. ´אֲשֶׁר בָּאָרֶץ הֵמָּה אַדִּירֵי וג ‘ the saints that are in the land, they (המה) are the nobles, in whom, ’ etc. **3\.** sometimes (though rarely) the defining adjunct is a pron. of 1 or 2 ps. as well as of 3 ps. In such cases it is strictly to be rendered *I who…, thou who*, etc.; [Ho 14:4](https://ref.ly/Hos14:4) אֲשֶׁר־בְּךָ יְרֻחַם יָתוֺם *thou by whom* the fatherless is compassionated ! [Je 31:32](https://ref.ly/Jer31:32) *I, whose* covenant they brake, [32:19](https://ref.ly/Jer32:19), [Is 49:23](https://ref.ly/Isa49:23), [Jb 37:17](https://ref.ly/Job37:17) f. *thou whose* garments are warm…, canst thou ? etc., [Psalm 71:19](https://ref.ly/Ps71:19), [71:20](https://ref.ly/Ps71:20), [144:12](https://ref.ly/Ps144:12) *we whose* sons, etc., [139:15](https://ref.ly/Ps139:15) my frame was not hidden from thee, אֲשֶׁר־עֻשֵּיתִי בַסֵּתֶר—*I who* was wrought in secret (\= *though I* was wrought in secret), [Ex 14:13](https://ref.ly/Exod14:13) for *ye who* have seen the Egyptians to\-day,—ye shall not see them again for ever! (cf. [Psalm 41:9](https://ref.ly/Ps41:9)). **4\.** the defining pron. adjunct is *dispensed with*—**a.** when אֲשֶׁר represents the simple subj. of a sentence, or the direct obj. of a vb.: so constantly, as [Gn 2:1](https://ref.ly/Gen2:1) the work אֲשֶׁר עָשָה *which* he made, [3:3](https://ref.ly/Gen3:3) the tree אֲשֶׁר בְּתוֺךְ הַגָּן *which* is in the midst of the garden, etc. **b.** after words denoting time, place, or manner, so that אֲשֶׁר then becomes equivalent to *when, where, why:* (*a*) [Gn 6:4](https://ref.ly/Gen6:4) אַחֲרֵי כֵן אֲשֶׁר afterwards, *when*, etc. (cf. [2 Ch 35:20](https://ref.ly/2Chr35:20)) [45:6](https://ref.ly/Gen45:6) there are still 5 years אֲשֶׁר אֵין חָרִישׁ *when* there shall be no plowing, [Jos 14:10](https://ref.ly/Josh14:10), [1 K 22:25](https://ref.ly/1Kgs22:25); after יוֺם or הַיּוֺם [Dt 4:10](https://ref.ly/Deut4:10), Ju [4:14](https://ref.ly/Judg4:14), [1 S 24:5](https://ref.ly/1Sam24:5) (v. Dr) [2 S 19:25](https://ref.ly/2Sam19:25), [Je 20:14](https://ref.ly/Jer20:14) al.; similarly [Gn 40:13](https://ref.ly/Gen40:13). (β) [Gn 35:13](https://ref.ly/Gen35:13) בַּמָּקוֺם אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר אִתּוֺ in the place *where* he spake with him, v:[14](https://ref.ly/Gen35:14), [39:20](https://ref.ly/Gen39:20), [Nu 13:27](https://ref.ly/Num13:27), [22:26](https://ref.ly/Num22:26), [Dt 1:31](https://ref.ly/Deut1:31) in the desert which thou sawest, *where* (accents Ke Di), [8:15](https://ref.ly/Deut8:15), [1 K 8:9](https://ref.ly/1Kgs8:9) (unless לוּחוֺת הַבְּרִית has here fallen out: v. LXX \& [Dt 9:9](https://ref.ly/Deut9:9)) [Is 55:11](https://ref.ly/Isa55:11) [64:10](https://ref.ly/Isa64:10) [Psalm 84:4](https://ref.ly/Ps84:4). So (γ) in אֶל אֲשֶׁר *to* (the place) *which* (or *whither*) [Ex 32:34](https://ref.ly/Exod32:34), [Ru 1:16](https://ref.ly/Ruth1:16); אֶל־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר *to* every (place) *whither* [Jos 1:16](https://ref.ly/Josh1:16), [Pr 17:8](https://ref.ly/Prov17:8); בַּאֲשֶׁר *in* (the place) *where* † Ju [5:27](https://ref.ly/Judg5:27), [17:8](https://ref.ly/Judg17:8), [17:9](https://ref.ly/Judg17:9), [1 S 23:13](https://ref.ly/1Sam23:13), [2 K 8:1](https://ref.ly/2Kgs8:1), [Ru 1:16](https://ref.ly/Ruth1:16), [1:17](https://ref.ly/Ruth1:17), [Jb 39:30](https://ref.ly/Job39:30), once only with שָׁם [Gn 21:17](https://ref.ly/Gen21:17); בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר *wheresoever* [Jos 1:7](https://ref.ly/Josh1:7), [1:9](https://ref.ly/Josh1:9), Ju [2:15](https://ref.ly/Judg2:15), [1 S 14:47](https://ref.ly/1Sam14:47), [18:5](https://ref.ly/1Sam18:5), [2 S 7:7](https://ref.ly/2Sam7:7), [2 K 18:7](https://ref.ly/2Kgs18:7); מֵאֲשֶׁר *from* (the place) *where* \= *whencesoever* † [Ex 5:11](https://ref.ly/Exod5:11), [Ru 2:9](https://ref.ly/Ruth2:9); עַל־אֲשֶׁר *to* (the place) *whither* (or *which*) [2 S 15:20](https://ref.ly/2Sam15:20), [1 K 18:12](https://ref.ly/1Kgs18:12); עַל־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר [Je 1:7](https://ref.ly/Jer1:7). (δ) …זֶה הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר this is the reason *that* or *why…* [Jos 5:4](https://ref.ly/Josh5:4), [1 K 11:27](https://ref.ly/1Kgs11:27). **c.** more extreme instances [Lv 14:22](https://ref.ly/Lev14:22), [14:30](https://ref.ly/Lev14:30), [14:31](https://ref.ly/Lev14:31), [Nu 6:21](https://ref.ly/Num6:21), [Dt 7:19](https://ref.ly/Deut7:19) (wherewith), [28:20](https://ref.ly/Deut28:20), [1 S 2:32](https://ref.ly/1Sam2:32) (wherein), [1 K 2:26](https://ref.ly/1Kgs2:26), Ju [8:15](https://ref.ly/Judg8:15) (about whom), [Is 8:12](https://ref.ly/Isa8:12) (where יאמר would be foll. normally by לוֺ), [31:6](https://ref.ly/Isa31:6) turn ye to (him as to) whom they have deeply rebelled, [47:15](https://ref.ly/Isa47:15), [Zp 3:11](https://ref.ly/Zeph3:11), [Ec 3:9](https://ref.ly/Eccl3:9), [1 K 14:19](https://ref.ly/1Kgs14:19) (\= how). **d.** it is dispensed with only in appearance after (´אָמַרְתִּי וג)אֲשֶׁר אָמַר followed by the words used, its place being really taken by a pron. in the speech which follows, as [Gn 3:17](https://ref.ly/Gen3:17) the tree *as to which* I commanded thee saying, Thou shalt not eat *from it*, [Ex 22:8](https://ref.ly/Exod22:8), [Dt 28:68](https://ref.ly/Deut28:68), Ju [7:4](https://ref.ly/Judg7:4) (זֶה) [8:15](https://ref.ly/Judg8:15) (where the noun repeated takes the place of the pron., cf. [Dt 9:2](https://ref.ly/Deut9:2)) [1 S 9:17](https://ref.ly/1Sam9:17) (זֶה):23 \+; cf. [2 S 11:16](https://ref.ly/2Sam11:16), [2 K 17:12](https://ref.ly/2Kgs17:12), [21:4](https://ref.ly/2Kgs21:4). **5\.** אֲשֶׁר sts. in poet. \= *one who, a man who* (*men who*), ὅστις, οἵτινες, [Psalm 24:4](https://ref.ly/Ps24:4), [55:20](https://ref.ly/Ps55:20), [95:4](https://ref.ly/Ps95:4), [95:5](https://ref.ly/Ps95:5), [Jb 4:19](https://ref.ly/Job4:19), [5:5](https://ref.ly/Job5:5), [9:5](https://ref.ly/Job9:5) (Hi) [15:17](https://ref.ly/Job15:17). **6\.** אֲשֶׁר occas. receives its closer definition by a subst. *following* it, in other words, its logical antecedent is inserted in the rel. clause: (*a*) in the phrase peculiar to Je., ´אֶל יר ´אֲשֶׁר הָיָה דְבַר י that which came (of) the word of ´י to Je. † [14:1](https://ref.ly/Jer14:1), [46:1](https://ref.ly/Jer46:1), [47:1](https://ref.ly/Jer47:1), [49:34](https://ref.ly/Jer49:34) (cf. Ew§ 334\); (*b*) [Ex 25:9](https://ref.ly/Exod25:9), [Nu 33:4](https://ref.ly/Num33:4), [1 S 25:30](https://ref.ly/1Sam25:30), [2 K 8:12](https://ref.ly/2Kgs8:12), [12:6](https://ref.ly/2Kgs12:6) לְכֹל :אֲשֶׁר־יִמָּצֵא שָׁם בָּֽדֶק Ez [12:25](https://ref.ly/Ezek12:25); cf. the Eth. usage Di:§ 201; (*c*) (antec. *repeated*) [Gn 49:30](https://ref.ly/Gen49:30) \= [50:13](https://ref.ly/Gen50:13), [1 S 25:30](https://ref.ly/1Sam25:30) (´י repeated), [Is 54:9](https://ref.ly/Isa54:9) (prob.) *as to which* I sware that, etc., [Am 5:1](https://ref.ly/Amos5:1) which I take up over you (as) a dirge. **7\.** ´אֲשֶׁר ל *that (belongs, belong*, *belonged) to*, is used **a.** either alone or preceded by כָּ־ל to express *(all) that (belongs) to*, as [Gn 14:23](https://ref.ly/Gen14:23) מִכָּל־אֲשֶׁר־לְךָ of all that is *thine*, [31:1](https://ref.ly/Gen31:1) מֵאֲשֶׁר לְאָבִינוּ of *that which was* our father's, [32:24](https://ref.ly/Gen32:24) \& sent over אֶת־אֲשֶׁר־לוֺ *that which he had*, \+ oft. **b.** as a circumlocution of the genitive, as [Gn 29:9](https://ref.ly/Gen29:9) עִם־הַצּאֹן אֲשֶׁר לְאָבִיהָ with the sheep *that were* her father's, [40:5](https://ref.ly/Gen40:5), [47:4](https://ref.ly/Gen47:4), [Lv 9:8](https://ref.ly/Lev9:8), Ju [6:11](https://ref.ly/Judg6:11), [1 S 25:7](https://ref.ly/1Sam25:7) הָרֹעִים אֲשֶׁר־לְךָ, [2 S 14:31](https://ref.ly/2Sam14:31) אֶת־הַחֶלְקָה אֲשֶׁר־לִי, [23:8](https://ref.ly/2Sam23:8), [1 K 1:8](https://ref.ly/1Kgs1:8), [1:33](https://ref.ly/1Kgs1:33) עַל הַפִּרְדָּה אֲשֶׁר־לִי upon mine own mule, v:[49](https://ref.ly/1Kgs1:49), [4:2](https://ref.ly/1Kgs4:2), [2 K 11:10](https://ref.ly/2Kgs11:10), [16:13](https://ref.ly/2Kgs16:13), [Ru 2:21](https://ref.ly/Ruth2:21); and esp. in the case of a compound expression depending on a single genit., as [Gn 23:9](https://ref.ly/Gen23:9), [40:5](https://ref.ly/Gen40:5), [41:43](https://ref.ly/Gen41:43) מִרְכֶּבֶת הַמִּשְׁנֶה אֲשֶׁר־לוֺ the chariot of the second rank *which he had*, [Ex 38:30](https://ref.ly/Exod38:30), Ju [3:20](https://ref.ly/Judg3:20), [6:25](https://ref.ly/Judg6:25), [1 S 17:40](https://ref.ly/1Sam17:40), [21:8](https://ref.ly/1Sam21:8) אֲבִיר הָרֹעִים אֲשֶׁר לְשָׁאוּל the mightiest of *Saul's herdmen*, [24:5](https://ref.ly/1Sam24:5) אֶת־כְּנַף־הַמְּעִיל אֲשֶׁר־לְשָׁאוּל, [2 S 2:8](https://ref.ly/2Sam2:8) Saul's captain of the host, [1 K 10:28](https://ref.ly/1Kgs10:28), [15:20](https://ref.ly/1Kgs15:20), [22:31](https://ref.ly/1Kgs22:31), [Je 52:17](https://ref.ly/Jer52:17), [Ru 4:3](https://ref.ly/Ruth4:3). **c.** with names of places (esp. such as do not readily admit the st. cstr.) Ju [18:28](https://ref.ly/Judg18:28), [19:14](https://ref.ly/Judg19:14) הַגִּבְעָה אֲשֶׁר לְבִנְיָמִין Gibeah (the hill) of Benjamin, [20:4](https://ref.ly/Judg20:4), [1 S 17:1](https://ref.ly/1Sam17:1), [1 K 15:27](https://ref.ly/1Kgs15:27), [16:15](https://ref.ly/1Kgs16:15), [17:9](https://ref.ly/1Kgs17:9), [19:3](https://ref.ly/1Kgs19:3), [2 K 14:11](https://ref.ly/2Kgs14:11). Comp. שֶׁל (q.v.) which in Rabb., like the Aram. \-דִּיל, ܕܺܝܠ, is in habitual use as a mark of the genitive.—N.B. In Aram. also דּי, ܕ, without ל, expresses the gen. relation, as מִלְּתָא דִי־מַלְכָּא, lit. the word, *that of* the king \= the word of the king. The few apparent cases of a similar use of אשׁר are, however, too foreign to the general usage of the language to be regarded otherwise than as due to textual error: [1 S 13:8](https://ref.ly/1Sam13:8) read אֲשֶׁר אָמַר (or שָם [Ex 19:5](https://ref.ly/Exod19:5)) שְׁמוּאֵל (LXX εἶπε); [1 K 11:25](https://ref.ly/1Kgs11:25) supply עָשָה (LXX ἥν ἐποίησεν); [2 K 25:10](https://ref.ly/2Kgs25:10) supply אֵת *with* (as ‖ [Je 52:14](https://ref.ly/Jer52:14)); [2 Ch 34:22](https://ref.ly/2Chr34:22) read וַאֲשֶׁר אָמַר הַמֶּלֶךְ (cf. LXX) and those whom the king appointed (abbreviated from [2 K 22:14](https://ref.ly/2Kgs22:14)); cf. Ew§ 292 a, b with note. **8\.** אֲשֶׁר becomes, like Aram. דּי, ܕ, a **conj.** approximating in usage to כִּי: thus **a.** \= *quod*, ὅτι, *that*, subordinating an entire sentence to a verb of knowing, remembering, etc. (*a*) with אֵת [Dt 9:7](https://ref.ly/Deut9:7) forget not אֵת אֲשֶׁר הִקְצַפְתָּ *the fact that* (\= *how*) thou provokedst, etc., [29:15](https://ref.ly/Deut29:15), [Jos 2:10](https://ref.ly/Josh2:10), [1 S 24:11](https://ref.ly/1Sam24:11), [24:19](https://ref.ly/1Sam24:19), [2 S 11:20](https://ref.ly/2Sam11:20) know ye not אֵת אֲשֶׁר־יֹרוּ *how* they shoot from off the wall ? [2 K 8:12](https://ref.ly/2Kgs8:12), [Is 38:3](https://ref.ly/Isa38:3) \+ oft. As subj. In [1 K 8:33](https://ref.ly/1Kgs8:33) (‖ [2 Ch 6:24](https://ref.ly/2Chr6:24) כִּי, cf. K v:[35](https://ref.ly/2Chr6:35); v:[37](https://ref.ly/2Chr6:37)) אֲשֶׁר may be rendered indifferently *because* or *when*. Once, similarly, אֵת אֲשֶׁר [1 K 8:31](https://ref.ly/1Kgs8:31) (‖אִם). **e.** perh. (exceptionally) \= כַּאֲשֶׁר, *as*, [Je 33:22](https://ref.ly/Jer33:22), [Is 54:9](https://ref.ly/Isa54:9) (sq. כֵּן; but כֵּן q.v. sts. stands without כאשׁר, \& אשׁר may in these passages connect with what precedes); acc. to some also [Je 48:8](https://ref.ly/Jer48:8), [Psalm 106:34](https://ref.ly/Ps106:34) (in a connexion where כַּאֲשֶׁר would be more usual: אֲשֶׁר may however be the obj. of אָמַר). In [1 S 16:7](https://ref.ly/1Sam16:7) אֲשֶׁר יִרְאֶה הָאָדָם rd. כַּאֲשֶׁר, v. Dr. **f.** combined with preps., אֲשֶׁר converts them into conjunctions: see below, בַּאֲשֶׁר, כַּאֲשֶׁר, מֵאֲשֶׁר. On its use similarly with אַחַר (אַחֲרֵי), מִבְּלִי, בַּעֲבוּר, עַל דְּבַר, יַעַן, לְמַעַן, כְּפִי, עַד, עַל, עֵקֶב, מִפְּנֵי, תַּחַת, see these words.—הַאֲשֶׁר, with ה *interrog.*, occurs once, [2 K 6:22](https://ref.ly/2Kgs6:22). *Note* I. אֲשֶׁר being a connecting link, without any perfectly corresponding equivalent in Engl., its force is not unfreq. capable of being represented in more than one way. See e.g. [2 S 2:5](https://ref.ly/2Sam2:5) (above **8 c**), [Is 28:12](https://ref.ly/Isa28:12) unto *whom* he said, or *for that* he said to *them*. *Note* 2\. The opinion that אֲשֶׁר has an asseverative force (like כִּי, q.v.), or introduces the apodosis, is not prob., being both alien to its general usage \& not required by the passages alleged. Render [Is 8:20](https://ref.ly/Isa8:20) either ‘ Surely acc. to this word will those speak *who* have no dawn, ’ or ‘…will they speak *when* (cf. supr. **8 d** [Dt 11:27](https://ref.ly/Deut11:27), [Jos 4:21](https://ref.ly/Josh4:21)) they have no dawn. ’

## I אֵת (id: BDB00950)

\[Str853] I. אֵת, with makk. אֶ־ת, with suff. אֹתִי; אֹֽתְךָ, אֹֽתְכָה † [Nu 22:33](https://ref.ly/Num22:33), אֹתָךְ, אֹתָכָה † [Ex 29:35](https://ref.ly/Exod29:35), fem. אֹתָךְ; אֹתוֺ etc.; 2 pl. אֶתְכֶם, once אֽוֺתְכֶם [Jos 23:15](https://ref.ly/Josh23:15); 3 mpl. regularly אֹתָם, rarely אֶתְהֶם † [Gn 32:1](https://ref.ly/Gen32:1), [Ex 18:20](https://ref.ly/Exod18:20), [Nu 21:3](https://ref.ly/Num21:3), Ez [34:12](https://ref.ly/Ezek34:12), [1 Ch 6:50](https://ref.ly/1Chr6:50), once אֽוֺתְהֶם Ez [23:45](https://ref.ly/Ezek23:45); 3 fpl., on the contrary, regularly אֶתְהֶן (13 t.), once אֹתָן Ez [16:54](https://ref.ly/Ezek16:54) (also אֽוֺתְהֶן Ez [23:47](https://ref.ly/Ezek23:47), אֹתָ֭נָה [Ex 35:26](https://ref.ly/Exod35:26), אוֺתָ֭נָה Ez [34:21](https://ref.ly/Ezek34:21)); forms with *cholem* also oft. written *plene:*—the **mark of the accusative**, prefixed as a rule only to nouns that are *definite* (Moab. *id.*, Ph. אית i.e. אִיַּת (Schrödp. 213 f.); Aram. יָת freq. in Targum; Syr. ܝܳܬ very rare as mark of accus. (for which ܠ is preferred), but used often in the sense of *substance* οὐσία, also in that of *self*, e.g. ܒܝܳܬܶܗ *per se, reapse*, ܠܝܳܬܶܗ *sibi ipsi*, PS1640 f., Sam. ࠉࠕ; Ar. إِيَّا, only used with sf., when it is desired to emphasize the pronoun, e.g. Qor 1:4 WAG i. § 189\. \[Eth. uses ኬይኣ *kīyā* similarly, Di:§ 150 a; but it is dub. if this is etymologically akin.] The primitive form will have been *’iwyath*, orig. a subst. with foll. gen., Olp. 432; whether ultim. a parallel development with אוֺת *sign* from √ אוה is uncertain: Ol WAG i. § 188 LagM i. 226 affirm, NöZMG 1886, 738 doubts. In Heb. the ground\-form is אוֺת; the forms with *ē, e* being abbreviated. In postB Heb., used in combination with another prep.: thus בְּאוֺתוֺ הַיּוֺם \= Bibl. בַּיּוֺם הַהוּא, בְּאוֺתָהּ הַשָּׁעָה; or as a nomin., e.g. אוֺתוֺ הָאִישׁ \= Bibl. הָאִישׁ הַהוּא).

 **1\.** As mark of the accus. prefixed to substs. defined either by the art. (or כֹּל), or by a genitive or pron. affix, or in virtue of being proper names: **a.** with transitive verbs, [Gn 1:1](https://ref.ly/Gen1:1), [1:16](https://ref.ly/Gen1:16), [1:29](https://ref.ly/Gen1:29), [1:30](https://ref.ly/Gen1:30), [2:11](https://ref.ly/Gen2:11), [4:1](https://ref.ly/Gen4:1), [4:2](https://ref.ly/Gen4:2), [9:3](https://ref.ly/Gen9:3) (:אֶת־כֹּֽל) etc. Similarly אֶת־מִי *whom* (in particular), [Jos 24:15](https://ref.ly/Josh24:15), [1 S 12:3](https://ref.ly/1Sam12:3), [28:11](https://ref.ly/1Sam28:11), [Is 6:8](https://ref.ly/Isa6:8) al. (but never אֶת־מָה); also with זֶה [Gn 29:33](https://ref.ly/Gen29:33), [44:29](https://ref.ly/Gen44:29), [1 S 21:16](https://ref.ly/1Sam21:16), [1 K 22:27](https://ref.ly/1Kgs22:27) \+, זאֹת [Gn 29:27](https://ref.ly/Gen29:27), [2 S 13:27](https://ref.ly/2Sam13:27) \+, אֵלֶּה [Gn 46:18](https://ref.ly/Gen46:18), [Lv 11:18](https://ref.ly/Lev11:18), [Is 49:21](https://ref.ly/Isa49:21) \+. So pretty uniformly in prose; but in poetry את is commonly dispensed with. By the use of את with the pron. affix, a pron. can at once, if required, be placed in a position of emphasis; let the order of words from this point of view be carefully noticed in the foll. passages: [Gn 7:1](https://ref.ly/Gen7:1), [24:14](https://ref.ly/Gen24:14), [37:4](https://ref.ly/Gen37:4), [Lv 10:17](https://ref.ly/Lev10:17), [11:33](https://ref.ly/Lev11:33), [Nu 22:32](https://ref.ly/Num22:32) *thee* I had slain, and *her* I had kept alive, [Dt 4:14](https://ref.ly/Deut4:14), [6:13](https://ref.ly/Deut6:13), [6:23](https://ref.ly/Deut6:23), [13:5](https://ref.ly/Deut13:5), Ju [14:3](https://ref.ly/Judg14:3) אוֺתָהּ קַח לִי take for me *her*, [1 S 14:35](https://ref.ly/1Sam14:35), [15:1](https://ref.ly/1Sam15:1), [18:17](https://ref.ly/1Sam18:17), [21:10](https://ref.ly/1Sam21:10) אִם־אֹתָהּ תִּקַּח־לְךָ קָ֔ח if thou wilt take *that*, take it, [1 K 1:35](https://ref.ly/1Kgs1:35), [14:9](https://ref.ly/1Kgs14:9), [Is 43:22](https://ref.ly/Isa43:22), [57:11](https://ref.ly/Isa57:11), [Je 9:2](https://ref.ly/Jer9:2). So הַאוֺתִי † [Je 5:22](https://ref.ly/Jer5:22), [7:19](https://ref.ly/Jer7:19). It also sometimes enables the reflexive sense to be expressed (elsewhere נַפְשָׁם) [Je 7:19](https://ref.ly/Jer7:19), Ez [34:2](https://ref.ly/Ezek34:2). Rarely with a subst. which is undefined (Ew§ 277 d 2 Ges§ 117, 1, R. 2\), as [Ex 21:28](https://ref.ly/Exod21:28), [Nu 21:9](https://ref.ly/Num21:9), [Lv 20:14](https://ref.ly/Lev20:14), [1 S 24:6](https://ref.ly/1Sam24:6), (but v. Dr) [2 S 4:11](https://ref.ly/2Sam4:11), [18:18](https://ref.ly/2Sam18:18), [23:21](https://ref.ly/2Sam23:21); or which, though definite, is without the art., [Gn 21:30](https://ref.ly/Gen21:30), [2 S 15:16](https://ref.ly/2Sam15:16), [Lv 26:5](https://ref.ly/Lev26:5), [1 S 9:3](https://ref.ly/1Sam9:3) (so [Nu 16:15](https://ref.ly/Num16:15)) [Is 33:19](https://ref.ly/Isa33:19), [41:7](https://ref.ly/Isa41:7), Ez [43:10](https://ref.ly/Ezek43:10) (for further exx. v. Ew *l. c.*) **b.** with a *passive* verb (Ges§ 121\. 1 Ew§ 295 b) conceived as expressing neutrally the action in question, and construed accordingly with an *accus.* of that which is its real object: exx. occur with tolerable frequency from [Gn 4:18](https://ref.ly/Gen4:18) (J) וַיִּקָּרֵא אֶת־שְׁמוֺ חֲנֹךְ and there was called (\= one called) his name Enoch, [17:5](https://ref.ly/Gen17:5) (P), [21:5](https://ref.ly/Gen21:5) (E), [27:42](https://ref.ly/Gen27:42), [2 S 21:11](https://ref.ly/2Sam21:11), [1 K 18:13](https://ref.ly/1Kgs18:13), [Ho 10:6](https://ref.ly/Hos10:6) etc., to [Je 35:18](https://ref.ly/Jer35:18), [38:4](https://ref.ly/Jer38:4), [50:20](https://ref.ly/Jer50:20), Ez [16:4](https://ref.ly/Ezek16:4), [16:5](https://ref.ly/Ezek16:5), [Est 2:13](https://ref.ly/Esth2:13) (cf. DrJPh xi. 227 f.): also with pass. vbs. of filling (Ew§ 281 b), as [Ex 1:7](https://ref.ly/Exod1:7) \+. **c.** with *neuter* verbs or expressions, esp. such as involve the idea of *regarding*, or *treating*, appy. by a constr. κατὰ σύνεσιν (rare), Jo 22:l7, [2 S 11:25](https://ref.ly/2Sam11:25), [Ne 9:32](https://ref.ly/Neh9:32) (cf. [1 S 20:13](https://ref.ly/1Sam20:13) Dr). Once after אֵין, [Hg 2:17](https://ref.ly/Hag2:17); אֵין אֶתְכֶם אֵלַיֽ. **d.** poet. (si vera l.), after an abstr. noun used with a verbal force, † Hb [3:13](https://ref.ly/Hab3:13) ([Am 4:11](https://ref.ly/Amos4:11), [Is 13:19](https://ref.ly/Isa13:19), [Je 50:40](https://ref.ly/Jer50:40) מַהְפֵּכָה exerts a verbal force, like the Arab. *nom. verbi* \[v. WAG i. § 196, 43]; and [Nu 10:2](https://ref.ly/Num10:2), Ez [17:9](https://ref.ly/Ezek17:9) לְמַסַּע, לְמַשְאוֺת are Aramaizing infinitives: cf. Ew§ 239 a). **2\.** את marks an accus. in other relations than that of direct obj. to a verb: **a.** with verbs of motion (very rare) [Nu 13:17](https://ref.ly/Num13:17), [Dt 1:19](https://ref.ly/Deut1:19), [2:7](https://ref.ly/Deut2:7) (to ‘ walk the wilderness ’); denoting the goal Ju [19:18](https://ref.ly/Judg19:18), Ez [21:25](https://ref.ly/Ezek21:25) (Ew§ 281 d, n., 282 a 1\). **b.** denoting time (duration), also very rare: [Ex 13:7](https://ref.ly/Exod13:7), [Lv 25:22](https://ref.ly/Lev25:22), [Dt 9:25](https://ref.ly/Deut9:25). **c.** expressing the accus. of limitation (rare): [Gn 17:11](https://ref.ly/Gen17:11), [17:14](https://ref.ly/Gen17:14), [1 K 15:23](https://ref.ly/1Kgs15:23). **3\.** Chiefly in an inferior or later style, אֵת (or וְאֵת) is used irregularly, partly (α), as it would seem, to give greater definiteness (so esp. וְאֵת) at the mention of a new subject (when it may sometimes be rendered *as regards*), or through the influence of a neighbouring verb (a cstr. κατὰ σύνεσιν), or by an anacoluthon, partly (β) as resuming loosely some other prep. Thus (α) [Ex 1:14](https://ref.ly/Exod1:14), [Nu 3:26](https://ref.ly/Num3:26), [3:46](https://ref.ly/Num3:46), [5:10](https://ref.ly/Num5:10) (with הָיָה: so Ez [35:10](https://ref.ly/Ezek35:10)) [Nu 18:21](https://ref.ly/Num18:21) b, [Dt 11:2](https://ref.ly/Deut11:2) (anacol.), [14:13](https://ref.ly/Deut14:13), [Jos 17:11](https://ref.ly/Josh17:11), Ju [20:44](https://ref.ly/Judg20:44), [20:46](https://ref.ly/Judg20:46) (contr. v:[25](https://ref.ly/Judg20:25); v:[35](https://ref.ly/Judg20:35)) [1 S 17:34](https://ref.ly/1Sam17:34) (v. Dr) [26:16](https://ref.ly/1Sam26:16), [2 S 21:22](https://ref.ly/2Sam21:22), [2 K 6:5](https://ref.ly/2Kgs6:5), [Is 53:8](https://ref.ly/Isa53:8) (prob.), [57:12](https://ref.ly/Isa57:12), [Je 23:33](https://ref.ly/Jer23:33) (but rd. rather with LXX Vulgate אַתֶּם הַמַּשָּא) [27:8](https://ref.ly/Jer27:8), [36:22](https://ref.ly/Jer36:22), [38:16](https://ref.ly/Jer38:16) Kt, [45:4](https://ref.ly/Jer45:4) b, Ez [16:22](https://ref.ly/Ezek16:22), [17:21](https://ref.ly/Ezek17:21), [20:16](https://ref.ly/Ezek20:16), [29:4](https://ref.ly/Ezek29:4) b, [43:7](https://ref.ly/Ezek43:7) (LXX Co prefix הֲרָאִיתָ) [44:3](https://ref.ly/Ezek44:3), [Zc 8:17](https://ref.ly/Zech8:17), [Ec 4:3](https://ref.ly/Eccl4:3), [Dn 9:13](https://ref.ly/Dan9:13), [Ne 9:19](https://ref.ly/Neh9:19), [9:34](https://ref.ly/Neh9:34), [1 Ch 2:9](https://ref.ly/1Chr2:9), [2 Ch 31:17](https://ref.ly/2Chr31:17). In [1 S 30:23](https://ref.ly/1Sam30:23), [Hg 2:5](https://ref.ly/Hag2:5) prob. some such word as *remember* is to be understood. (β) [Je 38:9](https://ref.ly/Jer38:9), Ez [14:22](https://ref.ly/Ezek14:22) b, [37:19](https://ref.ly/Ezek37:19) b, [Zc 12:10](https://ref.ly/Zech12:10); סָבִיב אֵת [1 K 6:5](https://ref.ly/1Kgs6:5), Ez [43:17](https://ref.ly/Ezek43:17) strangely (in 1 K LXX om. the clause: so StaZAW 1883, 135\).—In [1 K 11:1](https://ref.ly/1Kgs11:1) וְ is merely *and also, and especially* (v. וְ); v:[25](https://ref.ly/1Kgs11:25) is corrupt (rd. with LXX זאֹת הָרָעָה אֲשֶׁר עָשָה הֲדָד); Ez [47:17](https://ref.ly/Ezek47:17), [47:18](https://ref.ly/Ezek47:18), [47:19](https://ref.ly/Ezek47:19) rd. similarly for ואת, זאֹת: see v:[20](https://ref.ly/Ezek47:20).—For some particulars as to the use of את, see A. M. WilsonHbr. vi. 139 ff. 212 ff. (who, however, confuses it sts. with II. אֵת). For denoting the pron. obj. of a vb., את with suff. preponderates relatively much above the verbal affix in P, as compared with JE Dt Ju S K (v. ## II אֵת (id: BDB00951)

\[Str854] II. אֵת, **prep.** with—with makk. אֶ־ת, with suff. אִתִּי, אִתְּךָ, אִתְּכֶם etc. (also, however, אֽוֺתְךָ, אוֺתוֺ, and similarly מֵאֽוֺתְךָ, מֵאוֺתוֺ etc.), first in [Jos 10:25](https://ref.ly/Josh10:25), [14:12](https://ref.ly/Josh14:12), next [2 S 24:24](https://ref.ly/2Sam24:24); then repeatedly (but not exclusively) 1 K 20–2 K 8, \& in Je Ez, e.g. [1 K 20:25](https://ref.ly/1Kgs20:25) (but v:[23](https://ref.ly/1Kgs20:23) אִתָּם) [22:7](https://ref.ly/1Kgs22:7), [22:8](https://ref.ly/1Kgs22:8), [22:24](https://ref.ly/1Kgs22:24) (beside מֵאִתִּי) [2 K 1:15](https://ref.ly/2Kgs1:15), [3:11](https://ref.ly/2Kgs3:11), [3:12](https://ref.ly/2Kgs3:12), [3:26](https://ref.ly/2Kgs3:26), [6:16](https://ref.ly/2Kgs6:16) (beside מֵאִתּוֺ) [8:8](https://ref.ly/2Kgs8:8), [Je 2:35](https://ref.ly/Jer2:35), [10:5](https://ref.ly/Jer10:5), [16:8](https://ref.ly/Jer16:8), [19:10](https://ref.ly/Jer19:10), [20:11](https://ref.ly/Jer20:11), Ez [2:6](https://ref.ly/Ezek2:6), [10:17](https://ref.ly/Ezek10:17), [23:23](https://ref.ly/Ezek23:23), [37:26](https://ref.ly/Ezek37:26) (v. infr. **1 d;** also [Is 59:21](https://ref.ly/Isa59:21), contr. [Gn 17:4](https://ref.ly/Gen17:4): on שָׁכַב אֹתָהּ [Gn 34:2](https://ref.ly/Gen34:2) al., v. sub שָׁכַב, \& cf. DrSm ii. 13, 14\) prep. denoting **proximity** (syn. עִם; Ph. את, e.g. CISi. 3, 8 לא יכן לם משכב את רפאם let there not be for them a resting\-place *with* the shades; As. *itti* (perh. akin to *ittu* ‘ side, ’ DlPr 115 Hpt KAT2. 498; but cf. NöZMG ’86, 738 f.). Not found as yet in the other cogn. languages: but cf. Eth. እንተ ’ *enta,* towards, which supports the view; that אֵת is for ’ *int* \[cf. תֵּת, תִּתִּי], perh. from √ אנה *to meet* Olp. 431 PrätZMG ’73, 643 LagM i. 226\).

 **1\.** Of companionship, *together with:* [Gn 6:13](https://ref.ly/Gen6:13) behold, I destroy them אֶת־הָאָרֶץ *together with* the earth, [11:31](https://ref.ly/Gen11:31), [12:4](https://ref.ly/Gen12:4) \+ oft., esp. with *verbs of* dwelling, abiding, going, etc., as Ju [1:3](https://ref.ly/Judg1:3), [14:11](https://ref.ly/Judg14:11), [19:4](https://ref.ly/Judg19:4), \& in the phrase הָעָם אֲשֶׁר אִתּוֺ Ju [4:13](https://ref.ly/Judg4:13), [7:1](https://ref.ly/Judg7:1), [9:33](https://ref.ly/Judg9:33), [9:48](https://ref.ly/Judg9:48), [1 S 14:20](https://ref.ly/1Sam14:20), [30:4](https://ref.ly/1Sam30:4) etc.; thou, and thy sons …:אִתָּֽח *with thee* [Gn 6:18](https://ref.ly/Gen6:18); similarly (3rd Pers.) [7:7](https://ref.ly/Gen7:7), [7:13](https://ref.ly/Gen7:13), [8:18](https://ref.ly/Gen8:18), [9:8](https://ref.ly/Gen9:8) al. (charact. of P: DrIntr. 124\); הִתְהַלֵּח אֶת־הָאֱלֽהִים to walk *with* God, i.e. to have him as a companion (sc. by adopting a course of life pleasing to him) [Gn 5:22](https://ref.ly/Gen5:22), [5:24](https://ref.ly/Gen5:24), [6:9](https://ref.ly/Gen6:9) (cf. הִתְהַלֵּח אֵת lit. [1 S 25:15](https://ref.ly/1Sam25:15));—*by the side of, like* [Is 45:9](https://ref.ly/Isa45:9), *equally with* [Lv 26:39](https://ref.ly/Lev26:39), *in common with* [Je 23:28](https://ref.ly/Jer23:28) b (cf. עִם **1 e, f**). Hence, in partic.—**a.** *with* for the purpose of help: [Nu 14:9](https://ref.ly/Num14:9) אִתָּנוּ ´וי, [Jos 14:12](https://ref.ly/Josh14:12) (אוֺתִי, as [Je 20:11](https://ref.ly/Jer20:11)) Ju [1:19](https://ref.ly/Judg1:19), [2 K 6:16](https://ref.ly/2Kgs6:16), [9:32](https://ref.ly/2Kgs9:32) מִי אִתִּי מִי who is *on my side*, who ? כִּי אִתְּךָ אֲנִי [Is 43:5](https://ref.ly/Isa43:5), [Je 1:18](https://ref.ly/Jer1:18), [1:19](https://ref.ly/Jer1:19) \+; [Is 63:3](https://ref.ly/Isa63:3), [Psalm 12:5](https://ref.ly/Ps12:5) our lips are *with us, on our side;* in the phrase אֵת ´יַד פּ (הָֽיְתָה) [2 S 14:19](https://ref.ly/2Sam14:19), [2 K 15:19](https://ref.ly/2Kgs15:19), [Je 26:24](https://ref.ly/Jer26:24); נָשָא אֵת to bear *together with*, i.e. to assist [Ex 18:22](https://ref.ly/Exod18:22), [Nu 11:17](https://ref.ly/Num11:17). Thus Saul asks, מִי הָלַךְ מֵעִמָּנוּ who has gone *from* (those) *about* us ? but Jacob, speaking of the loss of Joseph, says, [Gn 44:28](https://ref.ly/Gen44:28) וַיֵּצֵא הָאֶחָד מֵאִתִּי and the one is gone *from with* me. מֵאֵת is accordingly preferred to מֵעִם in the sense of origination or authorship; מאת is not usual in the sense of מֵעִם **c**, nor מֵעִם in the sense of מֵאֵת **b.**.

## אָתָה (id: BDB00957)

\[Str857] † אָתָה **vb.** come (in Heb. only poet.) (Ar. أَتَى, Sab. אתו DHMZMG 1875, 597; 1888, 343, Aram. אֲתָא, ܐܶܬܳܐ)—**Qal** *Pf.* ´א [Dt 33:2](https://ref.ly/Deut33:2); אָתָא [Is 21:12](https://ref.ly/Isa21:12) v. Ges§ 75 R. 22; 1 pl. אָתָנוּ [Je 3:22](https://ref.ly/Jer3:22); *Impf.* יֶאֱתֶה [Jb 37:22](https://ref.ly/Job37:22), [Pr 1:27](https://ref.ly/Prov1:27); וַיֵּתֵא [Dt 33:21](https://ref.ly/Deut33:21) (\= וַיֶּאֱתֶה cf. Di Köi. 577\), וַיַּאת [Is 41:25](https://ref.ly/Isa41:25); sf. וַיֶּאֱתָיֵנִי [Jb 3:25](https://ref.ly/Job3:25); 3 fs. תֵּאתֶה [Mi 4:3](https://ref.ly/Mic4:3); 3 mpl. יֶאֱתָ֫יוּ [Jb 16:22](https://ref.ly/Job16:22) \+ 2 t.; וַיֶּאֱתָי\+וּן [Is 41:5](https://ref.ly/Isa41:5); *Imv.* mpl. אֵתָ֫יוּ [Is 21:12](https://ref.ly/Isa21:12) \+ 2 t.; *Pt.* fpl. אֹתִיּוֺת [Is 41:23](https://ref.ly/Isa41:23) \+ 2 t.;—*come*, of men [Dt 33:21](https://ref.ly/Deut33:21), [Psalm 68:32](https://ref.ly/Ps68:32), [Is 41:25](https://ref.ly/Isa41:25), [56:12](https://ref.ly/Isa56:12) *Imv. \= come now*, with hostile purpose [Jb 30:14](https://ref.ly/Job30:14), of men unto ´י [Je 3:22](https://ref.ly/Jer3:22) (sq. לְ) cf. [Is 21:12](https://ref.ly/Isa21:12); of ´י [Dt 33:2](https://ref.ly/Deut33:2); of ends of earth, etc., personif. [Is 41:5](https://ref.ly/Isa41:5); of time, morning [Is 21:12](https://ref.ly/Isa21:12), years [Jb 16:22](https://ref.ly/Job16:22); of weather [Jb 37:22](https://ref.ly/Job37:22); of beasts, to devour [Is 56:9](https://ref.ly/Isa56:9) (sq. inf.), of calamity [Pr 1:27](https://ref.ly/Prov1:27), [Jb 3:25](https://ref.ly/Job3:25) *come upon*, c. sf., of dominion [Mi 4:8](https://ref.ly/Mic4:8) (sq. עַד). *Pt.* pl. fem. as subst. *things to come*, future things [Is 41:23](https://ref.ly/Isa41:23), [44:7](https://ref.ly/Isa44:7), [45:11](https://ref.ly/Isa45:11). **Hiph.** *bring, Imv.* הֵתָ֫יוּ מַיִם [Is 21:14](https://ref.ly/Isa21:14) *bring water* (on form, for הֶאֱתוּ cf. Di EW:§ 141 a Ges§ 68, 2 R. 1\); [Je 12:9](https://ref.ly/Jer12:9) *bring beasts*, to devour.

> \[Str2978] † אִיתוֺן Qr, יאתון Kt, **n.m.** entrance, הָ֯יאִתוֺן Ez [40:15](https://ref.ly/Ezek40:15); Co rds. אתיון; cf. Sm Ol:§ 215 d.

> אִתַּי, אִתַי, אִיתִיאֵל v. sub II. אֵת.

> \[Str864] † אֵתָם **n.pr.loc.** (perh. \= Egypt. *Chetem*, cf. EbersGS 521 f. but LXX Ὀθομ, Ὀθωμ, cf. LagBN 54\) [Ex 13:20](https://ref.ly/Exod13:20) in Egypt, place on edge of desert, so [Nu 33:6](https://ref.ly/Num33:6), [33:7](https://ref.ly/Num33:7); אִדְבַּר אֵתָם [Nu 33:8](https://ref.ly/Num33:8).

> \[Str859] אַתֶּם v. sub אנת. p. 61

> \[Str865] אֶתְמוֺל v. sub תמל. p. 1069

## אתת (id: BDB00972)

אתת (? √ of following, meaning dubious. LagM ii. 254 proposes √ אנה, whence he derives also Ar. مَأْنٌ a tool used in tillage).

> \[Str855] † III. \[אֵת] **n.\[m.]** a cutting instrument of iron usually transl. ploughshare—sg. sf. אֵתוֺ [1 S 13:20](https://ref.ly/1Sam13:20); pl. אֵתִים [1 S 13:21](https://ref.ly/1Sam13:21), אִתִּים [Is 2:4](https://ref.ly/Isa2:4) \= [Mi 4:3](https://ref.ly/Mic4:3); sf. אִתֵּיכֶם [Jo 4:10](https://ref.ly/Joel4:10); acc. to Klo al. also [2 K 6:5](https://ref.ly/2Kgs6:5) אֶת־הַבַּרְזֶל, i.e. *the axe of iron.*

* **Associated Passages:** Micah 4:3; Joel 4:10; 1 Samuel 13:20; 1 Samuel 13:21; Isaiah 2:4; 2 Kings 6:5
